author: a. l. boyd
title: Nancy Mace calls for Bill Gates testimony and announces tech reform bills' passage - Berkeley Leader
text:
Rep. Nancy Mace, a U.S. Congresswoman representing South Carolina’s 1st district since 2021, posted a series of statements on her official social media account on February 4, 2026, addressing high-profile investigations and legislative developments.
In a post at 17:05 UTC, Mace wrote: “We’re calling for Bill Gates to testify under oath on his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein in front of the Oversight Committee. 3 million pages of Epstein documents were just released by the DOJ and the allegations are SICK. If these allegations are false, Bill Gates should https://t.co/qW6kzV2KDn”.
Later that day at 18:50 UTC, she commented on legal proceedings involving Ghislaine Maxwell: “We’re hearing Ghislaine Maxwell is planning to plead the 5th at her deposition on Monday. When a convicted sex trafficker pleads the fifth it isn’t about about self-incrimination any more, it’s self-preservation and not wanting to cross the rich and powerful people she”.
On legislative matters, Mace announced progress in government technology reform. At 20:09 UTC, she stated: “JUST IN: Our Modernizing Government Technology Reform Act AND our Cybersecurity Hiring Modernization Act have PASSED UNANIMOUSLY out of the House Oversight Committee. Your tax dollars are funding a government running on legacy technology and outdated hiring practices. Modern https://t.co/IwTEwc1W50”.
Mace has been active in federal legislative efforts since succeeding Joe Cunningham in Congress in 2021 and previously served in the South Carolina House of Representatives from 2018 to 2020. She was born in Fort Bragg, North Carolina in 1977 and currently resides in Charleston. Mace graduated from The Citadel with a Bachelor of Science degree in 1999.
